t.E310.agn: In 2014 EFSA set an acceptable daily intake (ADI) of 0.5 mg/kg body weight for propyl gallate and found no safety concern at current use levels.
t.E310.body: Gallate esters are broken down to gallic acid in the body (in the intestinal wall and also by gut bacteria). Most of the gallic acid is converted to 4-O-methylgallic acid and excreted in the urine, either free or conjugated with glucuronic acid.
t.E310.prod: Produced by the chemical reaction of gallic acid with alcohols.
t.E310.regx.0: Re-evaluated; ADI 0.5 mg/kg body weight/day, no safety concern at current uses.
t.E310.summary: A synthetic antioxidant derived from gallic acid. It delays rancidity in fats and is used in fats and fatty products.
t.E310.what: It is an antioxidant that delays the oxidation and rancidity of fats.
